item.title: MLB great Roger Clemens recalls George W Bush's iconic 9/11 World Series first pitch: 'A perfect strike'
item.description: Roger Clemens recalled George W. Bush's bulletproof vest, dress shoes, and Derek Jeter's advice before the iconic World Series first pitch after 9/11.
item.content:encoded:
President George W. Bush was America’s starting pitcher on Oct. 30, 2001.

In the wake of 9/11, the New York Yankees were playing the Arizona Diamondbacks in Game 3 of the World Series, and Bush threw out the first pitch. Roger Clemens, the Yankees’ starting pitcher that night, described the unforgettable moments that led up to Bush’s first pitch.

"I was actually in the bullpen warming up getting ready for the game with my pitching coach Mel Stottlemyre, and I told Mel let’s stop, I want to watch this," Clemens said during a recent appearance on Fox News’ "Fox & Friends."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"We have the best view, the whole stadium is going to light up, 55,000, whatever it was. You could see the snipers on top of the stadium, and he came out and threw a strike in front of the world, not just there at Yankee Stadium. It was for the world to see and it was nothing but spectacular."

Clemens was particularly impressed by Bush’s perfect strike, given the conditions of the mound and the equipment he had on.

"I could only imagine what President Bush was thinking when he was coming out of that dugout, bulletproof vest on. He threw from the top of the mound, and they dressed the mound with some dirt and mixture, and he’s in dress shoes. And so, to even go out there and not slip and be able to kick his leg up, like I said bulletproof vest and windup and throw a perfect strike right down Broadway," Clemens said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Clemens said he interacted with Bush in the clubhouse and gave the president a hug. The seven-time Cy Young Award winner said Bush was looking for a place to warm up when he received some sage advice from Derek Jeter.

"At the old Yankee Stadium you got to go out the clubhouse door and go to the right about 60-70 yards, and he went down there, and Derek Jeter, pretty well-known story, they had some small talk and Derek told him whatever you do Mr. President, don’t bounce it, you’re in Yankee Stadium, they’ll boo you," Clemens said.

"And I think he got a little nervous then. It was an awesome moment that I know I’ll never forget."

Clemens hopes that America never forgets 9/11 either.

"I can’t believe it’s been 25 years, I hope these kids that weren’t born then, I hope maybe our generation learned about Pearl Harbor that they learn about and keep 9/11 right there in the forefront of their mind," Clemens said.

For the 11-time All-Star, playing baseball during that time was a way to give grieving families and friends a chance to escape for a few hours each night. He recalled the late George Steinbrenner bringing family members and friends of those who were lost to the game.

For the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the New York Mets will play the Yankees on Friday night at Yankee Stadium.

item.title: Texas Rangers vs Seattle Mariners betting preview as Wild Card race heats up in final weeks
item.description: Jacob deGrom and the Texas Rangers face Logan Gilbert's Seattle Mariners in a key American League West matchup with MLB Wild Card implications.
item.content:encoded:
It has been only a couple of days since our last baseball game, and with football back, there will be a little less attention paid to the diamond. However, we shouldn't completely turn our back on Major League Baseball.

They are entering the last couple of weeks of games, and the Wild Card race is in full swing. With the playoffs on the horizon, let's get a bit of money in our pockets prior to their arrival. We have a good game between the Rangers and Mariners this afternoon.

The Texas Rangers are 72-74 and currently sit in second place in the American League West. This is most likely their best path to the postseason. There is still a chance they could capture a Wild Card spot. The Rangers are 1.5 games back of the final spot in that race as well, but they would need to get past the Guardians and the Blue Jays in order to advance. The Orioles are also hot on the Rangers' heels. Winning as much as possible is key over the final 16 games of their season.

Looking to steal this series and advance their standing a bit today is Jacob deGrom. When the Rangers got him on their roster, this is specifically the type of game they wanted him for. Although deGrom isn't quite the elite starter that he was years ago, he is still very good. For the season, deGrom is 10-9 with a 3.96 ERA and a 1.12 WHIP. This isn't a guy you'd expect to see with significantly different splits, but he has them. On the road, he has a 5.86 ERA, compared to just 2.46 at home. He has been awesome against the Mariners this season, with three starts covering 14 innings and two earned runs.

The Seattle Mariners will go down as one of the more disappointing teams in baseball. Expectations were extremely high for this team after having made it to the American League Championship Series. The team is loaded in the rotation; they made moves to address issues in the offseason, and the lineup, on paper, is one of the deepest in baseball. Sometimes things don't work out, and that appears to be the case for Seattle this season. They are 10 games under coming into today and are six games behind the Astros and 5.5 games out of the last Wild Card spot.

In order to try to keep their slim hopes alive today is Logan Gilbert. I've discussed Gilbert's numbers previously, but as a reminder, Gilbert is 11-9 with a 3.71 ERA and a 1.07 WHIP. His biggest downfall this season has been his performance at home this year. He has allowed 23 of his 26 homers in Seattle and has a 4.45 ERA in his home park. He has faced the Rangers three times this season and has allowed seven earned runs over 17 innings this year.

The total in this game is far too low. The books have it hung at 6.5 which is in line with pitchers of this caliber facing off. However, these pitchers are not pitching well in these situations. Gilbert has struggled at home, and deGrom has looked bad on the road this season. They have better numbers against their opposition, but I think we should see at least seven runs in this game. item.title: Fire aboard cargo ship undergoing repairs at busy Chinese port leaves 25 people dead, five more injured
item.description: A cargo ship called the Ocean Melody caught fire during repairs at Qingdao port, killing 25 of the 42 people on board the Liberian-flagged vessel.
item.content:encoded:
A cargo ship docked for repairs at a port on the northeastern coast of China caught fire Thursday, killing at least 25 people who were on board at the time, according to Chinese state media.

The ship was being fixed by Beihai Shipbuilding Co. in the port of Qingdao — one of the country's major shipping hubs — when it caught fire at approximately 11:15 a.m. local time, the Xinhua news agency reported.

A total of 42 people were on the vessel at the time of the blaze, and 12 of them were safely rescued, Xinhua reported. Five others were injured and taken to the hospital, where they are in stable condition.

CARGO SHIP ATTACKED BY SMALL CRAFT NEAR STRAIT OF HORMUZ, UK MARITIME AGENCY SAYS

Photos released by Xinhua identified the ship as the Ocean Melody. The ship-tracking website VesselFinder lists it as sailing under the Liberian flag.

The Associated Press reported that the fire was extinguished at around 2:30 p.m., a little over three hours after it started. Videos online showed plumes of white smoke billowing from the ship.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Chinese authorities have not said what sparked the blaze while the vessel was undergoing repairs.

TIM SHEEHY EXPOSES A 'SCARY' SHIPBUILDING COLLAPSE THAT LEAVES THE US VULNERABLE TO CHINA

China’s President Xi Jinping called for "intensified efforts" to provide support for those who were affected by the fire, Xinhua reported, adding that Premier Li Qiang said "trapped people" needed to be rescued.

Xi also called for ensuring "preventive measures are thoroughly implemented" and "resolutely prevent major and catastrophic accidents."

Beihai Shipbuilding is a subsidiary of the state-owned China State Shipbuilding Corporation, the world's largest shipbuilder. According to the company's website, its primary businesses are shipbuilding and ship repair.

Qingdao, in China's Shandong province, is one of the country's busiest ports and a major center for shipbuilding, shipping and international trade. The port handles millions of containers each year and is home to several large shipyards.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Republican sounds alarm on rising Dem star: 'This guy’s going to be a problem'
item.description: Mike Collins claims Jon Ossoff is using the Georgia Senate race as a Democratic Party springboard for a 2028 presidential run as a DSA candidate.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS — There’s a rising star in the Democratic Party that is generating buzz for a possible presidential run, but one Republican argues he’s the only thing standing in the way of a future "DSA candidate" in 2028.

Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., is running to unseat Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., in one of the most closely watched contests of this midterm election cycle. Ossoff has sought to nationalize their battle, focusing more on President Donald Trump and leaning into viral clips on social media to sell his message.

But Collins told Fox News Digital during the GOP’s midterm convention that Ossoff’s intentions extended beyond a second term representing the Peach State. Instead, Collins charged that Ossoff is eyeing the White House and using this cycle as a springboard to get there.

TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE SURVIVES GRUELING RUNOFF, ADVANCES TO HIGH-STAKES SENATE RACE

"This guy is nothing but a trust fund kid who's never had a real job in his life," Collins said. "And at the end of the day, and I think the whole puzzle has been put together now, you can put the pieces of this thing so easy."

"He caters to that far-left base, and at the end of the day, we've got to stop him in Georgia," he continued. "If we don't stop him in Georgia, this guy's going to be a problem for the entire country in 2028."

Those puzzle pieces were scattered throughout his voting record, which Collins said aligned over 90% of the time with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., through his support of progressives, like former Maine Senate Democratic nominee Graham Platner and Michigan Senate Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, and because the bulk of his campaign donations are from out-of-state.

'JESUS WAS A RADICAL': PROGRESSIVES INVOKE CHRIST TO SELL LEFT-WING AGENDA ON CAMPAIGN TRAIL

Collins contended that the final piece was when the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) opened their first permanent field office in Atlanta last month. The organization has not endorsed Ossoff.

"That just tells you, yes, Jon Ossoff is really running for president," Collins said. "He's going to be the DSA candidate. He uses Georgia as a platform to raise money."

Ossoff’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

OBAMA STRATEGIST TURNS ON RISING DEM STAR OVER VIRAL TRUMP ATTACK: 'GRATUITOUS AND UNNECESSARY'

He has previously thrown cold water on the notion that he was chasing the White House and told MSNOW last month, "I have zero interest in running for president in 2028, and, frankly, zero interest in the 2028 fantasy football right now."

The first-term senator is considered one of the most vulnerable incumbents on the Democrats’ Senate map this cycle, running in a state that Trump won in 2024 over former Vice President Kamala Harris by nearly three points.

Still, he has gained national attention over the summer for his speeches on the campaign trail, particularly when he needled Trump in a viral social media clip bringing into question his relationship with his executive assistant, Natalie Harp.

"He doesn't want to do the job," Ossoff said. "He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar."

That remark stoked a news cycle and earned him accolades from the likes of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., who noted that Ossoff was one of the top communicators on the trail when it came to targeting Trump.

item.title: How a podcast community helped restore the controversial 'Gator Bait' chant for Florida football team
item.description: James Di Virgilio and his "Gator Nation Football Podcast" rallied fans to write to Dr. Stuart Bell, helping revive the banned "Gator Bait" chant.
item.content:encoded:
For anyone who went through it, 2020 felt like living in a parallel universe.

The year was dominated by the Covid craziness that swept through the world as well as the myriad "cancellings" that took place, and college football in particular felt the effects of both.

Games and traditions alike were severely altered or outright shut down as a result of the pandemic and its accompanying lunacy, and the Florida Gators' football program especially felt the brunt of this.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S FIRST FULL SATURDAY IS HERE AND IT'S A CELEBRATION OF AMERICA AT ITS BEST

Sure, the Gators still played a ten game, All SEC slate, but access to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium was greatly limited, as the stadium which normally seats upwards of 90,000 fans on gameday had its attendance whittled down to less than 20,000.

In the wake of all of this, a tradition known affectionately around campus and throughout the community as "Gator Bait" was given the axe.

School officials cited "racial undertones" as the reason for removing the chant, linking back to late 19th and early 20th century depictions of using African-American children as bait for alligators.

The chant, at least in the context of the Florida football team, has much more innocent origins, being popularized in the 1990s by defensive back Lawrence Wright.

THESE ONCE-ANNUAL COLLEGE RIVALRIES USED TO DEFINE COLLEGE FOOTBALL AND NEED TO MAKE A COMEBACK ASAP

No one is more familiar with "Gator Bait" than James Di Virgilio, the popular podcast host of the "Gator Nation Football Podcast."

Di Virgilio and his co-host, Allen Williams, started the podcast back in 2014 as a break from the monotony and blind homerism that is abundant in the local sports talk radio shows around Gainesville, where the two reside.

Both are Florida graduates, and when they heard the news that "Gator Bait" was being shelved, Di Virgilio was perplexed.

"I think, like any Gator fan, it was surprising at first," said Di Virgilio. "As far as anyone could tell, no one who had ever used the chant at Florida... had any idea there could be any connection to anything other than a gator eating our opponents, so to speak, in a humorous way."

The GNFP host mentions other schools like LSU saying "Tiger Bait" as a rallying cry while receiving little to no backlash.

"I think it was a chant that many Gators (fans), especially those who are maybe 90s or 2000s Gators, have fond memories of chanting at opponents when you're winning national championships, etcetera, therefore it conjured up those memories of yesteryear," he opined.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS FINALLY BACK AFTER MONTHS OF NCAA LAWSUITS, NIL DRAMA AND CONGRESSIONAL FIGHTS

Despite the seemingly innocuous nature of the cheer, "Gator Bait" was officially banned in 2020 out of what Di Virgilio deemed "an abundance of caution" during a time of heightened scrutiny.

Meanwhile, in those years since the banning, the GNFP audience continued to grow.

Williams and Di Virgilio's analytical lens mixed with their obvious love and passion for the team they covered endeared them to tens of thousands of Gator fans, which presented them with a unique opportunity a few seasons ago.

At first, it started with a couple of comments here and there directed towards Di Virgilio about whether he thought "Gator Bait" could ever make a comeback.

OPINION: SPORTS IS ONE OF AMERICA'S GREATEST TRADITIONS AND A POWERFUL FORCE THAT UNITES US

"For two straight seasons, I basically polled our audience, which may or may not be representative of all of Gator Nation, to say 'does anybody really not want this?' Write to me," he explained.

Di Virgilio said in two full seasons of pushing for responses, he only got one message that was against bringing it back against hundreds that were in favor.

These messages, as he explained, came from a wide and diverse group of Gator fans, all of which cited very wholesome reasons for wanting the chant back in The Swamp.

"It wasn't just young people, it wasn't just old people. It wasn't just people of a certain skin tone," Di Virgilio mentioned. "It felt like it was a very pure, wholesome reason for wanting it."

Being a numbers guy, Di Virgilio had enough data to make his next move.

The University of Florida hired Dr. Stuart Bell to be their new president in July of this year, and since the decision to reinstate "Gator Bait" was up to the head man himself, Di Virgilio saw his opportunity to act.

"I had written to Dr. Bell a couple of weeks before we had everyone write to (him)," Di Virgilio said. "Here's my stance: I have limited information. You might have more information than I have. I would never want to do this if it was going to be divisive towards (other) Gators. I have no desire for that."

"But if you do the research and you find that this is something a majority of Gator fans want... then on your own merits, maybe think about reinstituting it."

With that, the die had been cast.

Countless fans of the GNFP took Di Virgilio's call to action to heart and wrote impassioned pleas to the university president asking for their beloved chant back.

They cited memories, tradition, and just the fact that it's a really catchy tune.

But as the emails piled up in Dr. Bell's inbox and the season drew nearer, something must have finally swayed the new president.

On the Friday before their first game against FAU, a clip was leaked of the Fightin' Gator Marching Band playing the familiar notes of "Gator Bait" on the practice field.

Lo and behold, the following day, 90,000 rabid Florida fans led a full-throated rendition of the once-banned cheer.

"Gator Bait" was back.

Di Virgilio wants to be very clear: he doesn't want the credit for bringing the chant back to The Swamp.

"I may have had 0.0001% to do with it," he explained. "Whether we were instrumental or not, someone else could have done it. I have no idea. We just felt like we wanted to push for something that brought back a lot of fond memories for us."

Regardless, he and his podcast community can certainly say they at least had a hand in ushering back one of the best cheers in college football.

"For me this is very apolitical," Di Virgilio said. "I think you want to do things that the majority of people want to do as long as it's not clearly violating any kind of legal or ethical boundary."

As he explains, Di Virgilio recognizes that not everything will be universally loved, including the "Gator Bait" chant.

Despite how popular the cheer's return has been on social media and in the Gator football community, some of the more vocal minority have bristled at the idea of "Gator Bait" making a comeback.

"I hope that if you're on the side of, you don't love it, you understand that those that (do) want it, want it for very traditional Florida reasons," said Di Virgilio. "And obviously, if you love it, you're not lording it over someone."

"Ultimately, we are all Gators."

In the end, it felt like a win for free speech, as the majority voiced their opinions and were rewarded accordingly.

It's a fact that is not lost on Di Virgilio.

"This is a really cool thing to know as podcasters, as a community of people, if you care about something you can take a second to write about it, on any side," he states.

"You may or may not have an influence, but at the end of the day, 'we the people,' so to speak, we do have a voice to share what we want... that's what this is really about. The beauty of articulate free speech and opinion, and also the willingness when you're wrong to just say, 'I was wrong.'"

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Welcome back, "Gator Bait."

item.title: Aaron Rodgers roasts 'gutless' ESPN's integrity for its Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel coverage 'hypocrisy'
item.description: Aaron Rodgers roasted ESPN for mostly ignoring the Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel story while prominently featuring Jed York's arrest on its homepage.
item.content:encoded:
Most NFL quarterbacks have plenty on their proverbial plate this time of year and aren't too worried about the league's scandals or the coverage of those by the landscape's most dominant sports network ESPN. Not Aaron Rodgers.

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is preparing for Sunday's season-opener against the Atlanta Falcons, but recently took time out to roast ESPN on the Not Just Football podcast with teammate Cam Heyward.

On the show Rodgers criticized the network's coverage, or rather, the lack of coverage of what he called the "intimate relations" between New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and former ESPN and Athletic reporter Dianna Russini.

"ESPN is really scared" of having him on the Pat McAfee Show to discuss that, Rodgers said.

STEELERS DEFEND AARON RODGERS' RIGHT TO VOICE OPINIONS AFTER ESPN FAUCI SEGMENT

Why?

"Because I can speak up and speak my mind," he said. "And that McAfee thing rattled their feathers, because I didn't just say that on McAfee's show, who is, honestly, I love Pat, and he's done more for that network than any other horrible show they have on there that they think is they should pay those guys doing it. But I also said, you're a gutless organization. Because they haven't said anything.

"They spend so much time on certain issues, but you won't talk one second about the Dianna Russini situation. What just happened? Uh, let's see, the owner of the Niners solicited a prostitute for [$160] in Ohio. That literally was the number one topic when you click on ESPN, right?"

"They rotate the eight stories or whatever they have. But they usually have, like, the one story they feature. That was a featured story. So you bring in how many millions of eyes to that situation. Why do you want to throw Jed York under the bus? I don't know."

49ERS OWNER JED YORK ARRESTED FOR 'ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION' IN OHIO, PLEADS NO CONTEST TO LESSER CHARGES

Well, one side done, flip ESPN over to cook the other side, Aaron ...

"But does that have the same effect as a reporter who, you know, has intimate relations with a coach?" Rodgers asked. "Who has a vote for MVP, who has a vote for Coach of the Year?

"There was the thing about Morgan Moses going from the Jets to New England that was posted a day early. How many other inside stuff was shared? There are a lot of insiders out there. Do they all have strong integrity? I don't know.

"But the fact that ESPN spent zero time on that story but Jed York gets popped ... and it's literally on the top of their roll ... That's hypocrisy."

Rodgers critics have claimed he dabbles in conspiracy theories and however one feels about that, he's not afraid to discuss a conspiracy theory about ESPN's lack of Russini coverage.

"I think there's a lot more to it," he said. "The NFL is gonna protect the shield. And I respect that. But they're gonna do it by all means necessary."

For the uninitiated, Russini and Vrabel were photographed at a Sedona, Arizona resort in April holding hands, embracing, spending time together at a pool and in a hot tub. Those photos and others pointing to a relationship beyond what is typical led The Athletic to conclude Russini's relationship with Vrabel was "in clear violation" of standards.

That is a bad look for everyone involved. And ESPN, who employed Russini from 2015 to 2023, is wholly in bed with the NFL. The league owns a 10% stake of ESPN.

"They got to be very very careful," Rodgers said.

item.title: Zohran Mamdani urged to skip New York City's 9/11 memorial: 'Vile antisemite'
item.description: Rep. Mike Lawler demands Zohran Mamdani skip the 9/11 memorial, citing the NYC mayor's ties to terror sympathizers and antisemitic rhetoric.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS – A House Republican representing the New York City suburbs is calling on Mayor Zohran Mamdani to skip the Sept. 11 memorial in downtown Manhattan.

"From my vantage point, I don't think he should be there, and I think most New Yorkers agree that he should not be there," Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., told Fox News and Fox News Digital. "Certainly, the 9/11 families and the first responders believe he should not be there."

Political rancor is threatening to cast a long shadow over this year's Sept. 11 remembrance events, marking 25 years since the tragedy that rocked the United States. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's past rhetoric and links to terror sympathizers are spurring intense backlash ahead of the city's events memorializing the World Trade Center attacks, with Republicans and people whose lives were changed by the attacks demanding he not show his face.

MAMDANI FACES GROWING 9/11 BACKLASH AS OLD POST RESURFACES AHEAD OF GROUND ZERO CEREMONY: 'IS THIS REAL?'

"I think Mayor Mamdani has proven himself to be a vile antisemite. I think he has associated with people who believe America deserved 9/11, and it's not just Hasan Piker. If you go look at many of the people that support his administration, they agree with that rhetoric. They agree with that philosophy," Lawler said.

An online petition led by family members of people killed on Sept. 11 — signed by over 100,000 people — has called on Mamdani to skip the memorial.

9/11 FAMILIES PUSH TO BAN MAMDANI FROM 25TH ANNIVERSARY REMEMBRANCE OVER 'HOSTILE' RECORD

"Mr. Mamdani has praised Brooklyn Imam Siraj Wahhaj, who has been linked to radical Islam, was named as an alleged co-conspirator in the 1993 World Trade Center bombing, and served as a character witness for the 'Blind Sheikh,' who was convicted in 1995 of plotting terror attacks against the United States," the petition said. "Mr. Mamdani has endorsed candidates such as Aber Kawas, who described 9/11 as an attack 'a couple of people did in the context of U.S. capitalism, racism, white supremacy, and Islamophobia,' and who also expressed sympathy for Ahmed Ferhani, who pleaded guilty to plotting to blow up a Manhattan synagogue."

Mamdani and other socialist candidates' association with far-left activist Hasan Piker has also seen intense scrutiny over Piker's past comments that the United States "deserved" the attacks, remarks that he promptly walked back at the time but continue to haunt him and his political circle. Mamdani himself has also condemned the comment.

Republican Study Committee Chairman August Pfluger, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital that Mamdani should not attend Sept. 11 memorial events "until he can... actually call out terror groups around the world for what they want to do to this country, and that includes Hamas."

Hamas was not responsible for the Sept. 11 attacks, for which al Qaeda took credit, but Hamas has recently been front-and-center for perpetuating the Oct. 7, 2023, terror attack in Israel.

"These people are really a cancer to the freedoms that we fought for, and they do not represent the American values that our founders set up and that we have had for 250 years," Pfluger said of Mamdani and his allies.

MAMDANI DROPS MASSIVE 9/11 RECORDS TROVE AS OLD CLAIMS ABOUT GROUND ZERO COME UNDER FIRE

Both he and Lawler spoke with Fox News Digital on the sidelines of the 2026 GOP midterm convention in Dallas.

Mamdani's office recently launched an online portal allowing city residents to access roughly 170,000 pages of local government records on Sept. 11, which appear to show city officials misled the public about air quality following the attacks.

Fox News Digital reached out to the New York City mayor's office for comment.

item.title: Alcohol tied to surprising cancer death pattern in adults under 55, researchers find
item.description: Alcohol-attributable cancer deaths in the United States more than doubled from 1990 to 2023, with colorectal cancer surpassing liver cancer in younger men.
item.content:encoded:
Annual U.S. cancer deaths tied to alcohol consumption more than doubled over a three-decade period, according to a recent study led by researchers at the Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine.

The findings, published in The Lancet Regional Health — Americas and presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology Annual Meeting in Chicago, revealed that alcohol-attributable cancer deaths jumped from 11,361 in 1990 to 23,126 in 2023.

Researchers analyzed more than 30 years of data from the Global Burden of Disease study to track the trends.

BEER, WINE OR LIQUOR? MASSIVE STUDY REVEALS WHICH WAS LINKED TO LOWER DEATH RISK

While alcohol has long been classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer, surveys show that awareness of its link to cancer remains limited.

"The most surprising finding was the breadth of alcohol’s potential impact across cancer types," Chinmay Jani, M.D., corresponding author of the study and chief fellow in hematology and oncology at Sylvester, told Fox News Digital.

"Although its relationship with liver cancer is widely recognized, its contribution to cancers such as colorectal, esophageal, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancer is less understood by the public."

CANCER DOCTOR REVEALS 5 HABITS THAT MAY REDUCE DISEASE RISK AND IMPROVE OUTCOMES

The research showed that older adults and men bore the highest overall burden of alcohol-related cancer deaths. Among older men, liver cancer was the primary cause of alcohol-attributable mortality, followed closely by esophageal and colorectal cancers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Breast cancer was the leading cause of alcohol-related cancer deaths among women overall, the study found.

Among younger adults between the ages of 20 and 54, colorectal cancer emerged as the leading cause of alcohol-attributable cancer deaths in men and the second leading cause in women, surpassing liver cancer in both groups.

The authors noted that the findings carry significant weight for public health messaging, particularly because general awareness surrounding alcohol's connection to various cancers remains low compared to known risks like tobacco use.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Because no minimum "safe" level of alcohol has been established, researchers said drinking less may help lower long-term cancer risk.

Because the study used existing national data rather than following individuals over time, researchers couldn’t determine each person’s exact drinking habits or account for every lifestyle factor.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

As a result, the findings show a strong association between alcohol use and cancer deaths, but they cannot prove that alcohol directly caused those deaths or establish a specific "safe" drinking limit.

"What this study makes clear is that alcohol-related cancer risk is not limited to one disease or one group of people," Gilberto Lopes, M.D., senior author and chief of the Division of Medical Oncology at the Miller School, told Fox News Digital.

"As physicians and cancer researchers, we have an opportunity to help patients understand that alcohol is a modifiable risk factor and that even small, informed changes can be part of a broader strategy to reduce cancer risk in our community."

item.title: WWE broadcaster Corey Graves hypes Triplemania 34 before Night 1 in Las Vegas
item.description: Triplemania 34 brings Lucha Libre AAA to the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on Friday, featuring Rey Mysterio vs. Omos and key WWE crossovers.

Triplemania 34, the premier event for Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide and better known as AAA, will take place in the United States for the first time. Night 1 will be held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on Friday and will showcase some of the best pro wrestling the sport has to offer. Night 2 will take place at Arena CDMX in Mexico City on Sunday.

The spectacle will showcase the talents who regularly perform on AAA programming on Saturday nights with a handful of familiar WWE stars mixed in.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

For pro wrestling fans who may not have tuned into AAA in the past or have and are unsure about what Triplemania is all about, commentator Corey Graves broke it down in a recent interview with OutKick Dropkick. He compared the style and colorful nature of Lucha Libre to that of the Savannah Bananas.

"So, I think most people would be familiar with WrestleMania. Most people, if you're not a pro wrestling fan, you're familiar with that brand. It's been massive for over 40 years. This is about to be the 34th installation of Triplemania, and Lucha Libre in Mexico is yes professional wrestling as we know it in America or around the globe, but it's very different. It's a unique cultural touchstone," he said. "There are bright colors and incredible action, and there's a lot of stuff that you will see on Raw or SmackDown including superstars who are heavily influenced by the Lucha Libre style. It's not exactly like you see on WWE, but it's the same.

"And I've used the analogy quite a few times lately because I'm a big baseball fan. If you're a Major League Baseball fan, WWE is Major League Baseball. AAA, to me, is sort of, and I mean this in the best way possible, like the Savannah Bananas. It's still baseball. All of the things that you know and love about baseball still take place. It's just through a very different lens. It's about these insane characters and costumes and pageantry and the action. You have a lot of people who can't sit through a nine-inning major league game who will spend their last dollar on tickets to go see the Savannah Bananas because it's an event. It's a happening. That's kind of how Lucha has always been in Mexico. And now this is an opportunity to bring that to an American audience in Las Vegas. And a lot of people, Savannah Bananas aren't for them, but they still like baseball. You get both. It's kind of the closest way I can explain it without betraying everything."

Graves said fans want to be a part of the action even though they may not fully understand the long history of Lucha Libre in Mexico.

Essentially, it’s all about being there.

"There’s incredible things. It's about moments. It's about memories," he said. "It's less about statistics and long-term records, etc. But it's about being there and just enjoying what's happening. And that's what AAA has become over the last year to me. You just want to be part of it even if you don't fully understand it.

"And I wouldn't expect a lot of our audience to — that's sort of my job, to sort of bring everybody along and explain to them why these characters are important and what they mean and why it is different, and it's important to me to maintain some difference. You don't want to lose that flavor. You don't want to lose the essence of Lucha Libre. We can clean up the production. We can sprinkle in a few WWE superstars here and there. But at its core, it's still Lucha Libre and TripleMania is AAA's WrestleMania."

It’s been a busy 18 months for WWE and Las Vegas.

WWE held WrestleMania 41 and 42 at Allegiant Stadium in 2025 and 2026 respectively. Now, they’re bringing in high-octane action back to the city with one of the biggest events on the wrestling calendar.

Originally, the event was set to take place at the Luxor. But WWE and AAA were forced to move venues because of the interest in the event.

"This is just me speaking off the top of my head. I can't say this with any sort of authority, but I would assume it shows the higher-ups, the people who make these decisions as to where to book the shows, when to book them, what to pour our resources into, specifically the fact that we were originally booked to be at the Luxor Hotel, and within days we were forced to move to the MGM Grand Garden Arena for capacity purposes because there was such a demand," Graves told OutKick Dropkick.

"Now, obviously, there's a heavy Latino population around Las Vegas but hopefully it's showing that English-speaking audiences as well are learning or curious about this new product. It's available for free every Saturday night on YouTube if you're in the United States or around most of the globe, obviously, we have television in Mexico and into Central and South America, but no matter where you are, Saturday nights 10 o’clock, you can tune into this and see what it's about. And it's such a visual product. And I say that almost discrediting myself because my job is to explain why it's important, but you can put it on mute and you can just watch and be captivated by the masks and the costumes and there's so much pageantry in Lucha. It's really, not that there isn't in WWE, it's just different. It's a completely different animal."

Night 1’s card features a bout between Rey Mysterio – the AAA general manager – and Omos. If Omos wins the match, he will be welcomed back to AAA. But if he loses, he will be forever shunned. Dominik Mysterio is set to be in Omos’ corner, while El Grande Americano will be behind Rey Mysterio.

Dominik Mysterio and El Grande Americano are pulling double duty to a point. The two will be featured on the Night 2 card as Mysterio defends the AAA Mega Championship against El Grande Americano.

item.title: Americans born on 9/11 mark 25 years with acts of service, trading personal celebration for honor
item.description: William Faber stopped celebrating his 9/11 birthday at age 10, choosing volunteer service over parties to honor those lost in the terror attacks.
item.content:encoded:
William Faber celebrated his Sept. 11 birthday as any young child would — but after learning about the significance of the day around age 10, he made the choice to spend the anniversary serving others rather than celebrating himself. 

Faber's story and several more are spotlighted in Fox Nation's new special following Americans born on Sept. 11, 2001, as they now turn 25 years old.

"Born on 9/11: 25 Years with Harris Faulkner" shares stories of how a birthday intertwined with one of the darkest days in American history has influenced lives marked by service, faith and community. The documentary examines the lives of individuals who have given back to their communities as they grew up. 

FRANK SILLER: 'I LOVE YOU, BROTHER' -- THE 9/11 LOSS THAT INSPIRED A MISSION OF SERVICE

Roughly 13,000 babies were born across the U.S. that day, Faulkner said Tuesday on "Outnumbered."

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: 9/11 IS JUST A HISTORY CHAPTER FOR A NEW GENERATION OF AMERICANS

Faber told her that, ever since his parents told him the story of 9/11, he has held his birthday parties on a different date.

"My parents... wanted to protect my feelings, the birthday, make sure I was able to celebrate, have fun. And then, as I got to be 10 years old, they told me the story. And so, ever since that day, I really haven't celebrated my birthday on that day," Faber said.

He made the choice out of respect for a family friend who died that day and the others who lost their lives in the terror attack.

"I want to volunteer, I want to give back to the community on that day. I'd rather not celebrate, I'd rather just do something to help the community as a whole," said Faber.

item.title: For 'horrible moment,' Bush White House thought US military shot down Flight 93
item.description: Condoleezza Rice recalled the tense moment she and George W. Bush believed Flight 93 had been shot down while coordinating responses in a bunker.
item.content:encoded:
Former President George W. Bush discussed his memories of 9/11 with his former secretary of state, Condoleezza Rice, ahead of the 25th anniversary of the attacks this week.

Bush and Rice said they both remember sitting in a bunker in the hours after the attacks, coordinating the U.S. domestic response. Rice recounted how they were working to ground civilian flights across the country and said at one point they thought the U.S. military had shot down United Airlines Flight 93.

"I do want to say one thing to Gen. [Daniel] Caine, because something in what you said, our paths crossed in a strange way. So you mentioned that you heard that as the president, you have to understand the hard decisions that this man had to make, just like that. And one of them was what would happen if a plane was not properly identifying itself, because every plane had become a missile," Rice said.

FLIGHT 93 HERO'S DAD WARNS 'ENEMIES FROM WITHIN' AIM TO DESTROY AMERICA AT THE BALLOT BOX

"And so we were trying to land, I remember Norm Mineta, the transportation secretary, trying to land planes on a legal pad, yellow pad, legal pad. But you'd given the order through the vice president that should a plane not squawk properly, it should be shot down. Gen. Caine, we thought initially, standing in that bunker, that Flight 93 had been shot down," she continued.

9/11 MUSEUM UNVEILS EXHIBITION FOR GENERATION TOO YOUNG TO REMEMBER THE ATTACKS: 'CALLED EVERYBODY TO LEAD'

"Yeah, I thought it was the same thing," Bush said.

"And there was this horrible moment where the vice president kept trying to get confirmation as to what had happened. And for about 10 minutes we thought we'd shot down a civilian aircraft. And that always, to me, represented just how hard the decisions were that you had to take under a lot of pressure," Rice said.

The event, called, "A Legacy of Service: America at the 25th Anniversary of 9/11," saw Bush host many members of his 2001 administration in Texas.

As part of the 25th anniversary commemoration, Bush painted 16 works of art that "reflect on the courage, sacrifice, and resilience that emerged from one of the most defining moments in American history," that will be displayed at Freedom Hall at the Bush Museum through September.

Fox News' Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

item.title: Team USA coach Kara Lawson speaks out on prognosticators after dominant FIBA World Cup win over Hungary
item.description: Kara Lawson dismissed FIBA's power rankings after Team USA women's basketball demolished Hungary 108-56 in the World Cup quarterfinal match.
item.content:encoded:
Team USA women’s basketball coach Kara Lawson dismissed outside opinions after the Americans routed Hungary 108-56 in the FIBA Women’s World Cup quarterfinal Thursday.

During the postgame press conference, Lawson was asked if a recent power ranking provided her team with any added motivation entering the final stage of the tournament.

Lawson admitted she did not know about the ranking, but addressed those who may have more confidence in France, which appeared to be the more dominant team during group play.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"This is a big tournament, this is the World Cup, and it’s okay for people to have opinions on who they think is going to win and who they think is going to lose and who they’re cheering for and who they’re going to boo. That’s a competition, I think that’s why we love sport, it’s why it’s so exciting," Lawson said.

"And now in this moment in women’s basketball you have more people than ever before that are giving their opinions and they’re making rankings and they’re doing that. That’s all great, we clearly don’t talk about any of that inside our bubble, and we really just focus on what we need to do.

ITALY WOMEN'S BASKETBALL STAR TEARS INTO REF AFTER MISSING GAME-TYING SHOT VS US IN WOMEN'S WORLD CUP

"Worrying about someone else’s opinion doesn’t serve you, because it doesn’t change whether you can do it or not. It’s just someone’s opinion."

FIBA moved France ahead of the United States in its final "Smart Power Rankings" following the group stage. The Americans fell to second after narrowly escaping Italy with a 55-52 victory, their lowest-scoring World Cup performance since the introduction of the 3-point line in 1984.

CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK

The ranking also described the Americans’ on-court connections as a "work in progress." However, FIBA included a disclaimer stating that its rankings were "entirely subjective" and did not constitute an accurate ranking system.

"As far as France, what a wonderful team, and they’ve had an outstanding World Cup so far, so they should have a lot of people thinking they can do well," Lawson said.

France strengthened its case Thursday with a 90-61 quarterfinal victory over China. The French remain on the opposite side of the bracket, meaning they could only face the United States in the championship game.

One of the biggest factors affecting the outlook for Lawson’s team entering the knockout stage was concern over the starting lineup. Lawson did not directly address that debate following Thursday’s victory.

WNBA LEGEND BREANNA STEWART OPENS UP ON REPRESENTING AMERICA AT FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese once again came off the bench against Hungary. Lawson instead started Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young, Kahleah Copper, Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart.

Lawson's commitment to keeping her veteran starting lineup has drawn frustration from fans, especially on Wednesday after Lawson suggested to OutKick that she will be keeping the veteran lineup going into the final stage.

Still, the lineup worked against Hungary with obvious results.

The U.S. scored 36 points in the opening quarter and carried a 59-30 advantage into halftime. The Americans shot 59% from the field, made 12 of their 23 3-point attempts and recorded 31 assists on 40 baskets. Their 108 points were the most ever scored in a Women’s World Cup quarterfinal, while they became the first team to record at least 30 assists at that stage of the tournament, according to FIBA.

Collier led the Americans with 19 points and six rebounds. Every player on the U.S. roster scored, and five finished in double figures.

Clark narrowly missed her second double-double of the tournament, recording 10 points and a game-high nine assists in 20 minutes. Reese contributed nine points, six rebounds and three assists, while Bueckers added seven points and three assists.

The victory also extended the Americans’ World Cup winning streak to 34 games. The program has not lost in the tournament since falling to Russia in the 2006 semifinals.

The U.S. will face the winner of Thursday’s quarterfinal between Australia and Spain in Saturday’s semifinal. Lawson’s team is now two victories away from securing a fifth consecutive World Cup championship.

item.title: Rams' travel gamble could give 49ers the edge in Thursday Night Football's Australia opener
item.description: The 49ers flew to Melbourne a week early while the Rams landed Tuesday, creating a massive travel edge for Thursday Night Football in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
Goo’day mate, shall we throw a bet on the barby? If you don’t understand the reason for that opener, then you might want to double-check your location for this game. The NFL is heading to Australia for the game today between the 49ers and Rams, which means we have our first Thursday Night Football action of the new season.

The San Francisco 49ers had a rather disappointing end to their 2025 season. They went into the playoffs looking like one of the more complete teams in football, and they were rinsed by the Seahawks basically from opening kickoff. This year they come in healthy, but there are an awful lot of questionable designations next to their lineup. They have six players on offense, including Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle, listed as questionable.

Their defense isn’t looking much better, with five guys listed, including Nick Bosa. Fred Warner is healthy, though, so that’s a good sign. If the team is fully healthy, it should be among the better in football. Even when the 49ers haven’t been healthy, they’ve had a strong next-man-up attitude that has made them stay in contention.

INJURY BUG BITES 49ERS AGAIN AS TEAM LOSES KEY DEFENSIVE TACKLE DURING PRACTICE IN AUSTRALIA

The Los Angeles Rams are a super team. It is almost comical looking at their roster. If the Pro Bowl was a thing, you’d basically call this roster a Pro Bowl roster. They were the only team to put up a true fight against Seattle in the playoffs, and they lost a back-and-forth battle. In the offseason, they added Myles Garrett via trade, and then that drew Aaron Donald out of retirement. A bit of good fortune for the 49ers is that Donald will not suit up.

Offensively, the Rams are still one of the most elite teams in football. It hinges on the health of Matthew Stafford, but he is coming off of an MVP season and arguably the best one of his career. He still has Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to throw the ball to. The team is extremely deep, and the Rams have a creative coach that won’t let them rest on offense.

AARON DONALD WILL NOT TRAVEL TO AUSTRALIA FOR RAMS OPENER AGAINST 49ERS AS TEAM RAMP-UP PROCESS NOT COMPLETE

This game being in Melbourne does throw a wrench into the betting strategy. If it was in Los Angeles, the Rams would probably be -4.5 favorites, and you probably just take them and move on. Instead, the game is overseas. Travel plays a major factor in this game. The 49ers flew to Australia a week ago and will be completely adjusted to the time difference.

SEAN MCVAY EXPECTS EVERY RAMS PLAYER TO BE ON FLIGHT TO AUSTRALIA FOR WEEK 1, INCLUDING AARON DONALD

The Rams, however, flew on Tuesday. That means they essentially land, then sleep, wake up, and play football. It is a 14-16 hour flight. They are also leaving two hours after the game is over. It is an interesting strategy, but the team apparently doesn’t want them to adjust. Traveling internationally is difficult. I expect the Rams to start rather slowly. The 49ers should have the upper hand at least through the first half of the game, as the Rams' bodies will still be off. Give me the 49ers with the points in this game. I just don’t think the Rams will ever get the separation needed, but they should win the game.

item.title: Why being ‘fortunate’ is more than just a T-shirt slogan for former WWE star Mosh
item.description: The Headbangers' Mosh reveals how his WWE tag team wrestling career and thyroid cancer survival inspired the Live Fortunate lifestyle brand.
item.content:encoded:
Any pro wrestling fan who tuned into "Monday Night Raw" during the peak of the war between WWE (then the WWF) and World Championship Wrestling would likely see The Headbangers wreaking havoc on the tag team division.

Mosh and Thrasher were, surprisingly, only one-time tag team champions during their careers with the company. Since leaving WWE, Mosh has transformed into an entrepreneur outside the ring and created a premium lifestyle brand that not only reflects his wrestling career but his life as a whole.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

If you tell Chaz Warrington (Mosh) that he’s "lucky" to have been given the opportunities he’s had in his life, he will stop you in your tracks. He’s not "lucky," he’s "fortunate." The Live Fortunate brand he created carries a significance that goes beyond just a simple T-shirt slogan. It’s a mantra and a way of life he’s cultivated throughout his life.

"So, Live Fortunate is based around if you've ever worked hard for something in your life and someone's told you you're lucky, this brand's for you," he told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview. "I'm very fortunate in my life with my past with wrestling, and I work a lot with nonprofits here in South Florida and because I have my wrestling background and because of the nonprofits I work with, a lot of opportunities have popped up for me as far as going to black-tie events and being able to make an impact on the community.

"And then with wrestling, different interviews come up. I'm fortunate enough to where WWE calls me and I can go up to their Performance Center in Orlando (Florida) and work with the NXT kids. So, I look at all of that as things that I've worked for, that have become opportunities because I've worked hard and I've done the work. I've put the time in. I've done the grind of working early in the morning. With my sales job that I have, I cold-called in 100-degree weather in a suit, walking up and down the street, which all of that has cultivated into different opportunities I've been given and I've earned."

Warrington said he thought of it while at his camp. When one member of his group told him he was "lucky," he immediately said "luck has nothing to do with it," despite the T-shirt he was wearing at the time was a Lucky Brand clothing item.

He told the person he would be wearing a different T-shirt when he saw them next. He said he was creating the T-shirt when he realized that being fortunate meant more to him than just a word on some cloth.

"The more I started getting into it and I thought about it, I'm like, this isn't just a T-shirt. It signifies something," he recalled. "For instance, I have another shirt that has a rhinoceros on it and it says ‘Live Fortunate’ on it. And then there's all the different words of gratitude, opportunities, and earning things — it's all like within there.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"So, that's kind of the message behind the brand. If you've worked hard for anything and someone's told you you're lucky, you're not ‘really lucky,’ you're fortunate because you've earned that opportunity. It's a clothing line. More of a premium lifestyle brand that I'm looking at. It's basically the message of getting that across. That's kind of what the basis is behind it."

Warrington said he has been fortunate to be able to give back to his community as well through the Junior Achievement of South Florida, teaching kids about financial literacy and sharing his life experiences with the younger generation.

There’s another reason for Warrington to feel fortunate, too.

He’s a cancer survivor.

Warrington was diagnosed with thyroid cancer in 2017.

He told OutKick Dropkick that he wasn’t one to worry about something unless there was something to worry about and keeping that even-keeled mindset helped push any negative thoughts out of his head to stay focused on the task at hand.

"I think that mindset for me kind of helped. That with the fact that I was like, I'm young. I have a family I still need to take care of. I need to be here, and I just look at things from a positive side. I always try to find a silver lining in something. I don't look at something as my glass is half empty or half full – it’s always three-quarters full, and I can always fill it back up. So, I think that that's the part that really helped me pull through that.

"And it's funny because there's a lot of times I don't think of myself as a survivor. I am, but I don't really look at it that way because, for me, what I went through in my mind was relatively easy. Again, there was a problem, there was a fix, we moved on. There are so many other people out there, their cancer was a lot worse or who are going through a lot worse things than me. So, if I could get the opportunity to talk to them about just trying to stay in a positive mindset, to find the silver lining – the glass is always three-quarters full and you still have an opportunity to refill it. I think that's kind of what got me through that and the message that, when I do talk to people, I try to get across."

Warrington said he learned the mind truly is a powerful thing and may be something that doesn’t get enough credit.

He is now focused on helping others realize how fortunate they are in their own lives and maximize the mindset through that message.

item.title: Pilot rescued after World War II-era plane crashes at Pennsylvania airport
item.description: The World War II-era plane had been airborne just nine minutes before crashing at Heritage Field Airport in Pennsylvania, causing a fuel leak on site.
item.content:encoded:
A World War II-era plane crashed while attempting to land at a Pennsylvania airport Wednesday evening, trapping the pilot inside the overturned aircraft before police and an airport employee freed him, authorities said.

Limerick Township police responded to Heritage Field Airport around 7:17 p.m. and found the small aircraft upside down on the runway with the pilot, its only occupant, trapped inside.

An airport employee and officers freed the pilot from his parachute and pulled him from the plane, police said.

FIERY SAN DIEGO PLANE CRASH KILLS 2

"We got reports the pilot was trapped in the plane. On our arrival, they were pulling him out. So there was no extrication needed by the fire department," Limerick Township Fire Chief Ken Shuler told FOX29 Philadelphia.

The pilot was conscious and able to stand but had visible cuts, police said. He was treated at the scene by Freedom Valley Medical Rescue and taken to a hospital.

The pilot was transported to Reading Trauma Center and was alert and talking after the crash, according to FOX29. No further update on his condition was available.

The single-engine plane had taken off from Pottstown and was headed to Quakertown, the station reported, citing Limerick Township officials. It had been in the air for about nine minutes.

FATAL AIR AMBULANCE CRASH EXPOSES GROWING GPS DANGER FACING US FLIGHTS

The crash caused a fuel leak, according to the outlet, and firefighters remained at the airport to address the spill and watch for a possible fire.

Heritage Field Airport, formerly Pottstown Municipal Airport, serves private and recreational aircraft. The airport remained closed Wednesday night while crews handled the fuel leak and removed the plane.

Police said they notified the Federal Aviation Administration's Eastern Region Operations Center after the crash.

The cause of the crash was not immediately known, and police said aviation authorities are investigating.

item.title: British actress Lesley-Anne Down traded in LA’s fires and political leanings for a life in Georgia
item.description: Classic British actress Lesley-Anne Down traded in Los Angeles wildfires, Hollywood’s harassment and political leanings for a life in Georgia.
item.content:encoded:
After years of living along the Pacific coast in Malibu, British actress Lesley-Anne Down named California’s continuous wildfires and liberal-leaning politics as the reasons she and her family left the Golden State for a life in Georgia.

Down lived in southern California for decades after crossing the pond to pursue her Hollywood dream, but became so let down by the environment there — both natural and political — that she would eventually become a Southern belle.

But Down, now 72, perhaps best known for her film roles in 1976’s "The Pink Panther Strikes Again" and 1978’s "The Great Train Robbery," traded it all in for a serene life feeding the deer that frequent her residence outside Atlanta in what she described as the ultimate "suburban countryside."

PALISADES VILLAGE TO RE-OPEN, MARKING NEW MILESTONE FOR FIRE-DEVASTATED COMMUNITY

The actress and singer — known as one of Hollywood’s most beautiful women in the late ‘70s and ‘80s for her piercing blue eyes and striking features — was voted Britain’s Most Beautiful Teenager and had her breakthrough role in the British television series "Upstairs, Downstairs."

"I have to be very honest. I cannot think of a more lovely place to have brought up our first lot of kids, you know, who are now all in their middle and late 40s," Down told Fox News Digital, reflecting on her time living in the Point Dume and Trancas areas of Malibu. "It was just lovely."

Down, along with her husband, cinematographer and director Don E. FauntLeRoy, spent a lot of time in Malibu in the early ‘80s before they purchased their first house together on Point Dume. They lived there until 2020.

"I remember looking out the kitchen window and, like, three riderless horses just going out for a little trot," she said, recalling the beauty of Broad Beach at that time, which she would later refer to as "Rock Beach" because of all the erosion. "But then it began to change — the people and, quite frankly, the fires. The fires got worse and worse."

UNCONTAINED BRUSH FIRE IN NEVADA TRIGGERED BY HUMAN ACTIVITY; INFERNO GROWS TO 13K ACRES

During the first 10 years of living there, Down recalled only one fire in which she was actually evacuated. But then, not more than two years later, another fire required all of her friends in Corral Canyon to vacate their homes.

"We had a house full of fire victims, quite frankly, because who wants to sleep on a cot in Malibu High School? And we had a big house, so that was that," Down recalled, noting that her husband was often away working when the fires occurred.

The Woolsey fire in 2018 was the last straw. Down remembered getting a police escort over Kanan Dume Road, which she said "looked like the moon" at that point.

"And I said, I can’t take this anymore," she recalled, crediting her young son George, a typical Malibu-raised surfer dude at the time, with saving their home.

KIRK CAMERON PRAISES NASHVILLE'S 'GOOD VALUES' AFTER DITCHING CALIFORNIA OVER COST OF LIVING, POLITICS

Down and her husband had been talking for years about leaving the state but weren’t sure where to go. The growing frequency of California’s wildfires wasn’t the only factor; Down was also increasingly troubled by the state’s shift toward more liberal politics and policies. 

Earlier in her career, Down had also experienced her share of brushes with the industry’s casting couch.

"We’re in this politically correct world, and you can only be one thing, and you can’t be anything else," Down said, noting that because of this "politically very, very frightening world" that we live in, the United States is rushing at light speed toward what her native Britain has become.

"That’s always what’s happened, you know. America always follows suit from England, sort of, you know, eight to 10 years later," she said, making it a point to endorse fellow Brit and California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton to become the state’s next governor.

"He’s such a smart man," she said.

TRUMP-BACKED HILTON ADVANCES TO CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR GENERAL ELECTION

"Quite frankly, I don’t think I’ve ever made any secret of where I feel and where I land politically, even though I was not where I am politically when I was young, but I am now," Down said. "So, I think that the chances of me ever working — even if I wanted to — in this industry, because of my politics, are slim to none."

"God forbid, I was, you know, 35, and I wanted to work, and I needed to work. Guess what I’d have to do? I’d either have to be very brave and very poor, or I’d have to keep my trap shut and pretend that I’m something that I am not," she added.

But to every rule there is an exception, and for Down, that meant taking on the role of Margaret Thatcher in the 2024 biopic "Reagan," around the same time she, her husband and their son moved to the Atlanta area. It was a place that FauntLeRoy was familiar with due to work ties and where their son George, who wanted to work in the industry, could thrive.

For Down, the role in "Reagan" came out of the blue, and she described it as somewhat fortuitous because, as she put it, "COVID-19 left the pool of actresses smaller."

"In all honesty, in my entire life, I never really wanted to be in this industry. Life just happened. And then I was on a roller coaster and that is what happened to me," Down said, noting that she felt very much a part of the "old school" of Hollywood and never transitioned well to what she referred to as the "new school" of actors in town. And when she attempted that transition, she wasn't happy. 

NEW FOX NATION DOCUMENTARY CHRONICLES 20-YEAR JOURNEY BEHIND ‘REAGAN’ FILM

"It was not professional as far as I could see," Down said, noting how radically the industry had changed. "When I did ‘Reagan,’ everything that I’m saying to you is not true. ‘Reagan’ was very much ‘old school.’ The people were old school, everybody behaved old school, the etiquette … the group you were with was really marvelous."

"And so, you know, honestly and truly, if I could do a film or a job like that every so often, I’d do it, but they’re rare," she continued. The movie is returning to approximately 600 theaters for a wide re-release on Sept. 25.

For now, Down continues to enjoy domesticity, her community of neighbors whom she calls "intensely wonderful," and the deer that visit her daily.

"There’s one stag, and he’s not scared at all, and I have to tell him — I say, ‘Could you please stay away from me while I put the corn on the ground?’" Down explained in her distinctly polished but whimsical British tone.

'HERCULES' STAR KEVIN SORBO SAYS CALIFORNIA CAN KEEP ITS TAXES, TRAFFIC AND 'NEGATIVITY': 'I'M DONE'

While she’ll reminisce about those days in the Malibu sun, what Down — who grew up poor and had a father who instilled in her the belief that "nothing is free" — doesn’t miss are the fires or the politics.

She cites those "libbies" who can afford to say, "Everybody should have everything free," yet live in a society that needs the kind of money required to pay for all of those things.

It’s not even that she doesn’t take the left’s side on some things. She said it’s about how polarizing it has become to even talk about differing views.

"You can’t appear to be right-wing today, because if you appear to be on the right, or you have any right-wing political views whatsoever, they take that, and they twist it, and they use it to turn you, strangely enough, into some kind of Nazi, when really the reverse is true," Down explained.

"That’s a shame, I think. I was not happy with the fact that people couldn’t talk. I don’t like people screaming at me about nothing," she said. "So if you put the politics and the fires and the need for George to establish a life, that is the perfect storm and that’s why we’re here."

item.title: 9/11 hero Welles Crowther's firehouse president reveals what shaped the 'man in the red bandana'
item.description: Welles Crowther's volunteer firehouse shaped the hero who saved 18 lives on 9/11. Its president reveals how training and community forged the legend.
item.content:encoded:
When President Donald Trump awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom posthumously to Welles Crowther for his heroism during the 9/11 terrorist attack during a Tuesday ceremony, Crowther's mother Alison specifically mentioned the Upper Nyack, New York, volunteer firehouse where Welles got his training.

"Welles... would not have been able to do what he did as effectively on 9/11 if it had not been for the training and experience he gained as a member of Empire Hook and Ladder Company Number One of Upper Nyack," she said.

Crowther, as Empire Hook and Ladder Company Number One president David "Trevor" Gottlieb explained to Fox News Digital, was forged in the volunteer firehouse's traditions of community and sacrifice.

FIRST ON FOX: TRUMP’S 9/11 TRIBUTE TO FEATURE MASSIVE PIECE OF GROUND ZERO HISTORY AT WHITE HOUSE

"I joined in '88, he was five years younger than me so probably '93 is when he first started," Gottlieb told Fox News Digital.

"I was still away in college. I came back and worked with him from '93 on. Volunteer fire service is usually multi-generational, and Welles' father, Jefferson, was an ex-captain. He was our treasurer, just, you know, part of the fabric of the company. Kid's been coming down here since he could walk," Gottlieb said.

In the 25 years since the terrorist attacks on 9/11, Crowther's story has become something of a legend. Known as the "man in the red bandana," Crowther carried a red bandana on his wallet while working as a stockbroker in the South Tower. When the attack struck, he immediately leapt to action, helping usher people to safety as the building burned around him.

"Welles Crowther was in the towers. He was working for a trading firm that day. And he assisted with the rescue of at least 18, I think was the final count they got. Eighteen civilians that he helped lead to safety and ultimately lost his life doing that," Gottlieb said.

"I think what Welles' impression he left upon us was anything's possible. And when you're faced with, you know, 108 floors and the chaos and the destruction all around you, when you sit back and rely on your training, on how you were brought up, I think that makes your job much easier," he continued.

Gottlieb credited Crowther's instinct to help people without hesitation to his upbringing at Empire Hook and Ladder.

"This fire company is stocked with great people. We have five generations, some of the families go back in this company. And it's great to see the pride, the dedication, commitment to a community that exists when you have such a special place like this," he said.

"I would lay my life down for any one of them. And I think they would do the same for me," Gottlieb said of his firehouse family. "That's something that's kind of instilled in when you join here. And it's perfected throughout years and multi-generations of that behavior," he continued.

9/11 MUSEUM UNVEILS EXHIBITION FOR GENERATION TOO YOUNG TO REMEMBER THE ATTACKS: 'CALLED EVERYBODY TO LEAD'

Crowther's ultimate sacrifice was indicative not only of his upbringing in Empire Hook and Ladder, but of the spirit that inhabits all volunteer firefighters, Gottlieb argued.

"When you look at what happened that day, somebody made the decision to not run. They made the decision to stay and help. And they didn't ask if you're a Republican, a Democrat, a Muslim, a Jew, a Catholic," he told Fox News Digital.

"You're somebody who needs help. And the human spirit needs to continue that way. We have to focus on what brings us together, not what divides us," Gottlieb said. "And I think that's been kind of the driving force in the firehouse. For us to get more volunteers, we can't be a polarizing organization. We can't have sides. Our position is we're here to help the community."

"We are here to step up in the times that probably matter most and be part of something much bigger than ourselves," he added. "And when you learn to set that aside and you learn to live with those kinds of principles, I think it makes this job much easier because you know that – know – the guy next to you, the girl next to has your back and I have their back."

NYPD CHIEF: 9/11 HEROES’ LEGACY LIVES ON IN EVERY GENERATION OF OFFICERS

Gottlieb also pointed to two of Empire's other fallen firefighters, Harry Wannamaker Jr. and Joe Stach Jr., who he said both lost their lives due to health complications related to 9/11.

"We should never forget. We should never forget the sacrifice that everybody made, in particular Welles. But there was 343 other firemen that died. And then, since that time, we've lost two more members in Empire related to 9/11 diseases, Harry Wanamaker Jr. and Joe Stach Jr. And it's awful to see the scars that it leaves on families forever," he said.

MASSACHUSETTS TOWN CANCELS JULY 4 CELEBRATION CITING LACK OF 'ADEQUATE PUBLIC SAFETY STAFFING'

Gottlieb also urged people to follow in Crowther's footsteps and volunteer for their local fire departments.

"Volunteer fire service is hurting for people right now. Everybody's too busy to volunteer and I can't describe to you the feeling, right? You get to drive fire trucks, you get to play with some pretty cool tools. I encourage everyone to do this, make time, help any way you can because your community will be better for it," he said.

item.content:encoded:
