item.title: 9/11 hero’s memory preserved through massive effort to ‘do good’ for vets, first responders: ‘His legacy’
item.description: Tunnel to Towers' 343 Homes Initiative honors Stephen Siller and the 9/11 firefighters with mortgage-free homes for fallen first responders' families.
item.content:encoded:
On one of the darkest days in America’s history, New York City firefighter Stephen Siller strapped on his gear and ran through the Brooklyn Battery Tunnel to the collapsing Twin Towers, ultimately giving his life to save those caught in the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. Two and a half decades later, Tunnel to Towers, founded by Siller’s family, has continued his legacy through its commitment to "do good" for veterans and first responders and their families across the country.

Since its founding, inspired by Siller and his favorite quote, "While we have time, let us do good," Tunnel to Towers has provided more than 1,700 mortgage-free homes to the families of fallen service members and first responders, as well as to disabled veterans and first responders. The organization has also delivered housing assistance and support services to more than 20,000 homeless veterans and holds hundreds of events nationwide to honor America’s heroes and preserve the memory of those who lost their lives for future generations.

Tunnel to Towers CEO Frank Siller, the brother of the 34-year-old firefighter who gave his life on Sept. 11, previously warned in 2020 that America was "very close to forgetting the impact 9/11 had on our nation." Now, with anti-American sentiment on the rise and some online commentators belittling the Sept. 11 attacks or even justifying them, many worry the legacy of those who lost their lives, including the 343 members of the New York City Fire Department who made the ultimate sacrifice, will be forgotten.

Siller, however, has vowed that "Tunnel to Towers will never let that happen."

9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS

The Tunnel to Towers 9/11 Institute has helped to educate students from kindergarten through 12th grade on the "extraordinary heroism and goodness of everyday people" on Sept. 11, "while demonstrating the strength and resilience of America’s spirit." Its mobile 9/11 exhibit has traveled to nearly all 50 states as well as Canada.

This year, Tunnel to Towers launched its "Steel Across America" display, in which a 16,000-pound steel beam pulled from the wreckage of the World Trade Center traveled more than 10,500 miles to 35 stops across 21 states and the District of Columbia, culminating in New York City.

NEW 9/11 MUSEUM EXHIBIT AIMS TO CONNECT YOUNGER AMERICANS TO THE ATTACKS THROUGH POWERFUL ARTIFACTS

To mark the 25th anniversary, Tunnel to Towers also launched its 343 Homes Initiative this year to honor the 343 New York firefighters who died on Sept. 11. According to the group, this initiative will deliver 343 mortgage-free homes to the families of fallen service members and fallen first responders as well as to catastrophically injured service members across the country.

This initiative builds on Tunnel to Towers' "In the Line of Duty Programs," which have provided more than 1,700 mortgage-free homes to the families of fallen service members and first responders, as well as to catastrophically injured veterans and first responders. More than 220 of those homes have been custom "Smart Homes," modified to be fully accessible to catastrophically injured veterans and first responders.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

In a recent Fox News opinion piece, Siller put it simply: "Stephen’s life and heroic death serve as a reminder to us all to live life to the fullest and to spend our time here on earth doing good—this is his legacy."

item.title: Supreme Court again blocks Missouri from using Trump-backed congressional maps
item.description: The Supreme Court blocked Missouri's Republican-backed congressional map for a second time as a contempt hearing looms for Denny Hoskins this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court turned back another effort to use Missouri congressional maps supported by President Donald Trump.

"The application for stay presented to Justice [Brett] Kavanaugh and by him referred to the Court is granted," Thursday's ruling read.

The court's brief order was unsigned and gave no explanation, as is common when the justices handle emergency matters. No justice publicly dissented from the decision.

MISSOURI AG FILES PETITION ASKING SUPREME COURT TO REVIVE TRUMP-BACKED REDISTRICTING MAP

While the Missouri Supreme Court’s ruling paved the way for use of the old maps, the state’s Aug. 4 primary was already held under the new maps.

"After repeated legal victories defending Missouri’s fair and lawful map, this 11th-hour ruling pulls the rug out from under voters who already cast their primary ballots," RNC Election Integrity Communications Director Ally Triolo wrote in a statement. "Changing the rules mid-election is reckless and wrong."

The court’s decision came after U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark ordered Missouri to use the new map, conflicting with a unanimous ruling by the Missouri Supreme Court that said the districts had not legally taken effect and that the state’s older map should be used unless voters approve the changes.

Republican state officials have argued it would violate voters' federal rights to switch districts before the general election.

MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING

The Missouri Supreme Court also ordered Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins to appear at a contempt hearing Thursday, after he instructed local election officials to use the new districts. A federal judge declined to halt that hearing before the Supreme Court issued its order.

The redrawn map was approved by Missouri Republicans in 2025. It dismantles the Kansas City-based 5th Congressional District held by Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, D-Mo., by shifting portions of the seat into neighboring districts and extending the remainder into heavily Republican areas.

The way the map was designed gave Republicans a strong chance of winning seven of Missouri’s eight House seats, compared with the current six-to-two Republican advantage.

Opponents of the map, including the group People Not Politicians, submitted hundreds of thousands of petition signatures seeking a statewide referendum. The Missouri Supreme Court ordered that referendum to appear on the November ballot, meaning voters will decide whether the redrawn map can be used in future elections.

Republicans currently hold a 219-214 majority in the House, including one independent who caucuses with the GOP.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Henry Winkler addresses reported Tom Hanks tension after being fired from 1989 movie
item.description: Henry Winkler reveals he's still processing what went wrong with Tom Hanks after being fired from "Turner & Hooch" just 13 days into filming.
item.content:encoded:
Henry Winkler is opening up about the reported decades-long tension between himself and Tom Hanks, revealing he is still trying to understand what went wrong between them.

In a recent interview on "In Depth With Graham Bensinger," Winkler — who was fired as director of Hanks’ 1989 movie "Turner & Hooch" after 13 days of filming — addressed the situation that initially ignited the reported rift.

Winkler admitted he was not "suited" to direct the movie, but accepted the job after being handpicked by Disney executive Jeffrey Katzenberg.

TOM HANKS PUT 'BAND OF BROTHERS' STARS IN THEIR PLACE DURING BOOT CAMP 'MUTINY', NEAL MCDONOUGH REVEALS

"I went completely against my tummy, and it hit me in the face with a 2x4," Winkler said. "I now meet the puppies, and I meet with Tom [Hanks]... and I, at that time being insecure, I talked too much and I gave them direction. I [did] what I thought was my job, and I wanted to do it over again and apparently that p---ed them off."

Winkler said the situation came to a head just 13 days into filming.

SCOTT EASTWOOD SAYS HIS FATHER SENT KEVIN COSTNER HOME FROM SET WHILE FILMING 'A PERFECT WORLD'

"I’m called into [Katzenberg’s] office, and he said, ‘It’s not in the dailies,’" Winkler recalled. "I then go to the set. I get my things. I drive home. I’m fired as a director... I don’t handle it well. I’m devastated."

Winkler was replaced by director Roger Spottiswoode.

Winkler also revealed that Hanks later declined to give permission for a clip from his "Happy Days" appearance to be used in a retrospective about the sitcom.

"We did a retrospective on 'Happy Days,' and we wanted 60 seconds of Tom Hanks in his episode, and we did not get permission for that," Winkler said.

Hanks appeared on the sitcom in 1982, years before his movie career took off.

When asked what his "perspective" was on his relationship with Hanks, Winkler replied, "I am still working on my perspective."

Asked whether he believed the relationship could ever "repair itself," Winkler responded, "Sure."

'HAPPY DAYS' STAR SCOTT BAIO SAYS HE WAS ALMOST FIRED FROM ICONIC SERIES AFTER 'GETTING A BIG HEAD'

Winkler has previously spoken about the difficult experience while continuing to deny that he and Hanks had an outright feud.

SCOTT EASTWOOD TOLD SHIA LABEOUF 'I'M GOING TO WHOOP YOUR A--' DURING TENSE ON-SET CLASH

In comments to TMZ in 2020, which were later reported by Vanity Fair, Winkler said, "I don’t have a feud with Tom Hanks. What everybody says and what is true are two different things."

Winkler added that he had seen Hanks at the Screen Actors Guild Awards that year.

"It was beautiful," he said.

However, during an appearance on "Watch What Happens Live" a year earlier, a viewer called in and asked the "Barry" star about the reported feud.

"What was the real reason why you and Tom Hanks didn’t get along on the set of ‘Turner & Hooch,’ and did you ever wind up seeing that movie?" the fan asked.

Winkler detailed his firing before discussing his relationship with Hanks’ canine co-star.

"I got along great with that dog," he said. "Love that dog."

Host Andy Cohen then asked Winkler if he had gone to see the movie in theaters.

"I don’t even remember the title of that movie," Winkler said.

Hanks has not publicly commented on the reported tension between the two actors.

item.title: Dodgers place Shohei Ohtani on injured list ahead of push for third straight World Series title
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers placed Shohei Ohtani on the injured list with right arm discomofort on Wednesday, manager Dave Roberts announced.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are about to have a four-time MVP-size hole in their lineup.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced late Wednesday night that Shohei Ohtani will go on the injured list with right arm discomfort. The 32-year-old has missed six of the last seven games as he has managed lingering soreness in his right biceps and left knee for weeks, but he felt something in his arm after playing Monday.

"There was a swing Monday that he didn’t feel great on, hasn’t totally recovered from Monday," Roberts said before the game.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"In talking to Shohei, the doctors, the training staff, it’s the right thing to do. We tried to kick the can as much as we could."

Roberts insisted that if the postseason began Thursday, Ohtani would be in the lineup, and he expects Ohtani to come off the injured list on the 15th day. The two-way star will not travel with the team on its upcoming East Coast road trip.

"Let’s get his body feeling well and then slowly ramp back up because now we do have time," Roberts said.

Roberts said Ohtani will take a two- or three-day rest to "calm his arm down."

If Ohtani indeed returns on the 15th day of his stint on the injured list, he would return on Sept. 22, giving him just six games to reacclimate to live pitching again before the Dodgers begin their quest to win their third straight World Series title.

"It's certainly not ideal," Roberts admitted. "The most important thing is him being as healthy as possible, not compromising his swing, and kind of bet on that."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In hindsight, Roberts wished the team had put Ohtani on the injured list earlier when it gave him four days off to rest.

"I would love to go back and put him on the IL," Roberts said. "But I did feel at that moment in time, we all felt that giving him four days was sufficient. He was agreeable."

"The concern is that after four days (off) and then to take four at-bats and to feel something in an at-bat where we can’t keep going forward, I think that’s disappointing," Roberts said before the game.

The six-time All-Star was in the midst of another MVP-caliber season. In 130 games, he has a .277 batting average with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs while stealing 11 bases. As a pitcher, he was 8-2 in 14 starts with a sparkling 1.79 ERA in 85 2/3 innings pitched before being shut down because of the injury.

With Ohtani injured, Chicago Cubs superstar center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong now becomes the heavy favorite to win the National League MVP award.

To take Ohtani’s spot on the roster, the Dodgers called up top prospect Josue De Paula straight from Double-A. The 21-year-old will be the team’s designated hitter against the Miami Marlins.

The team has never called up a position player directly from Double-A, but Roberts is confident the organization’s 21-year-old top prospect from the Dominican Republic can handle the pressure.

"I think that our player development group is very confident in his ability to conduct an at-bat. You could argue that the talent in Double-A is similar to Triple-A as far as pure arms and arm talent," Roberts said. "We've seen him in camp for two or three years. He doesn't run from velocity. He controls the strike zone. This is just a good opportunity for him to kind of cut his teeth in the big leagues."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: TSA weighs major change to frustrating airport security rule for some travelers
item.description: TSA weighs whether to let PreCheck passengers bring full water bottles through airport security checkpoints using advanced CT scanners.
item.content:encoded:
Travelers could soon be allowed to bring full water bottles through some airport security checkpoints — a major shift from longstanding airport security restrictions.

The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is weighing whether to allow TSA PreCheck passengers to bring water bottles through security checkpoints, according to reports.

The change would apply to a select number of airports across the United States.

POPULAR PANTRY STAPLE COULD GET YOU STOPPED AT AIRPORT SECURITY UNDER LITTLE-KNOWN TSA RULE

Senior administration officials told CBS that the proposal would be limited to airports using advanced CT scanners capable of distinguishing between water and other liquids.

It is unclear which airports would participate.

While existing technology is capable of screening full bottles of liquid, TSA has not acquired it on the scale needed for a nationwide rollout, even for PreCheck passengers, according to CBS.

The agency also does not currently have the funding required for such an expansion, the outlet reported.

TSA PreCheck, which allows eligible travelers to use expedited security lanes and typically keep their shoes, belts and light jackets on during screening, generally costs less than $100 for a five-year membership, according to the agency.

The potential change drew a mix of enthusiasm and relief from travelers in an aviation-themed Reddit forum.

"Welcome to 2026, USA," one Redditor wrote.

item.title: Buffalo Bills' plan to feature Canadian anthem at stadium opener met with mixed reactions
item.description: Buffalo Bills will play "O Canada" at the Highmark Stadium opener, sparking heated debate among fans amid ongoing U.S.-Canada tariff tensions.
item.content:encoded:
The Buffalo Bills adding "O Canada" to the pregame festivities at the Highmark Stadium opener has fans singing two different tunes.

The team announced Wednesday that the Canadian national anthem will be played by The Barenaked Ladies before next Thursday's game against the Detroit Lions as the Buffalo region officially opens its new $2.2 billion stadium. Auliʻi Cravalho, the voice of "Moana," will sing "The Star-Spangled Banner."

As Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and President Donald Trump continue to battle it out over tariffs, the Bills will acknowledge their Canadian fans who cross the border to use their season tickets and spend their money in the United States. As of 2025, it was estimated that Canadians held 8,000 Bills season tickets. At that same time, 18% of Highmark Stadium personal seat license deposits were credited to Canadians.

CANADIAN PM TELLS TRUMP TO 'STOP TRYING TO BE TOUGH' IN TRADE FIGHT

What factors led to the Bills deciding to include "O Canada" in its plan for an historic night in Buffalo history? It's unclear. OutKick reached out to the Bills to ask that question, but we have yet to hear back from the team. We would also be interested to know if the Bills plan to make "O Canada" a permanent addition to Bills games or if this is a one-time deal.

Last year, even as Canada and Trump were feuding, the team was focused on making Canada a priority.

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

"Regardless of the climate, we’re going into Toronto," Pete Guelli, the Bills’ executive vice president and chief operating officer, told the New York Times last year. "The passion for the Bills in that market has not subsided at all with what’s been happening."

How are fans reacting to the news that the Canadian national anthem will be played at the Highmark opener? It's a mixed bag.

"I am Canadian. This is stupid. You shouldn’t be playing the Canadian anthem. We don’t deserve your kindness at this moment. God bless, America," one Bills fan wrote on X.

"As a Canadian season ticket holder I appreciate this. Might be unnecessary but given the stupidity happening between our respective national governments [its] a sign of goodwill," wrote another.

That said, it hasn't been sunshine and roses when the Star Spangled Banner has been played at Canadian sporting events. At the 2025 NHL 4 Nations Face-Off, Canadians booed the anthem in Montreal as an American flag was projected onto the ice. Then, this summer, Canadians booed the U.S. flag during a World Cup ceremony at a match in Toronto.

How will Bills fans react to an anthem being played when the teams on the field aren't from Canada? The prevailing theory is that fans will just go along with it because it's the neighborly thing to do, but that's to be seen.

Some Bills fans won't soon forget what nearly happened to their beloved team during the mid-2000s.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"They had no problem trying to steal our team. Asinine decision," Bills Mafia member Gary Castine wrote on X.

For those that might not remember, there was a time when the possibility of the Toronto Bills was a legitimate concern for fans. The Bills Toronto Series was played from 2008-2012 at the Rogers Centre. It was viewed as a test run for the NFL to relocate the team to Toronto.

TRUMP RENAMES LAKE ONTARIO ‘LAKE AMERICA’ AMID INTENSIFYING US-CANADA TRADE DISPUTE

The Bills finished the Toronto series with a 1-5 record, and the experiment was viewed as a disaster. Former starting center Eric Wood called the games "a joke."

For Castine, he hasn't forgotten what nearly happened to his team. "Why are you getting political? Stupid decision," he wrote to the Bills on X. "I’ve loved the Bills for 70 years and made 2 generations die hard bills fans. This sucks. Nothing against Canada but are they singing the USA national anthem at Maple Leaf games?"

They do, but only when a U.S. team is in town.

item.title: University of Tennessee condemns flyers appearing to celebrate Charlie Kirk assassination
item.description: Flyers at the University of Tennessee advertise a campus gathering celebrating Charlie Kirk's assassination anniversary, but the university is condemning it.
item.content:encoded:
The University of Tennessee-Knoxville is condemning messages that celebrate political violence after mysterious "Kirkaversery" [sic] flyers advertised a gathering apparently marking one year since Charlie Kirk’s assassination, declaring, "WE WILL CELEBRATE THE FIRST NEW YEAR AK (AFTER KIRK)."

The flyers, images of which circulated widely on social media and by Libs of TikTok, advertise an 8 p.m. Sept. 10 gathering on the HSS Lawn, an outdoor green space at UT Knoxville. But the university told Fox News Digital that it is not sponsoring an event related to Kirk’s assassination and that no organization has registered to use the location for such a gathering.

"The university is not sponsoring any event related to Charlie Kirk’s assassination, and no organization has registered to use the HSS Lawn or any other reservable space for any such event," a university spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement Wednesday. "At this time, the university has not determined whether the flyers are connected to anyone affiliated with UT."

PORTLAND TATTOO ARTIST ADVERTISES $50 ‘KIRKIVERSARY’ NECK TATTOOS ON ANNIVERSARY OF CHARLIE KIRK’S DEATH

The spokesperson added, "The University of Tennessee strongly condemns any message or activity that celebrates or makes light of violence or the loss of human life. We remain committed to ensuring our campus is a place that values civility and where human dignity is respected."
